etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin splendidus, from splendere (“to shine”) +‎ -idus (“adjective forming suffix”).

definitions.definition: Possessing or displaying splendor; shining; very bright.

quote.citation: 1875, Henry Watts, A Dictionary of Chemistry and the Allied Branches of Other Sciences:
quote.text: It is distinguished from xanthocobaltic nitrate by its crystalline form, and by yielding a splendid cinnabarred precipitate with a solution of iodine in potassium iodide  […]

definitions.definition: Gorgeous; magnificent; sumptuous; of remarkable beauty.
Brilliant, excellent, of a very high standard.

quote.citation: 1950, C. S. Lewis, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe:
quote.text: "We've fallen on our feet and no mistake," said Peter. "This is going to be perfectly splendid. That old chap will let us do anything we like."

quote.citation: November 2 2014, Daniel Taylor, "Sergio Agüero strike wins derby for Manchester City against 10-man United," guardian.co.uk
quote.text: Hart had to make two splendid saves as Van Persie and Di María took aim and Fellaini should really have done better with a headed chance.
